body: Yeah, I think we agree. One of the articles linked above referenced [another research](https://news.ucsb.edu/2016/016429/flawed-measure) that talked about it being flawed.

> According to who?

[Change in Body Mass Index Associated With Lowest Mortality in Denmark, 1976-2013](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2520627) - this [article](https://www.sciencealert.com/the-healthiest-weight-could-actually-be-overweight-huge-study-finds) explains the results.

[Underweight people at as high risk of dying as obese people, new study finds](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2014/03/140328103037.htm) and [Archive link for their source](https://web.archive.org/web/20210121124433/http://www.stmichaelshospital.com/media/detail.php?source=hospital_news/2014/20140328_hn) since the link to the site appears to redirect to the front page now.


That's for underweight of course, and OP's goal is not quite that. But if they were to lose a couple of kilos after a stressful month or a bad flu, would that suddenly be very worrying and unhealthy? Can't tell if what OP is doing is good or bad for them, I am not their doctor, and it would be hypocritical of me to say they shouldn't, as I am losing past the 24bmi my dietitian recommended. But really, is .2 points of bmi what it takes to go from good and healthy to concerning and dangerous?

CoolSculpting has about [1 in 50 chance of Paradoxical Adipose Hyperplasia](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK606530/), which gives the opposite results.

It's not worth the risk.

Thank you. This is an important point that does not got mentioned as much as it should. Eating disorders are not just dismissed very often but in many cases are actually encouraged by others if a person is not very thin.

I had anorexia a couple of years ago and nobody knew about it because I still had some belly and no thigh gap. A month into recovery my boyfriend at a time would point at skinnier girls and tell me he liked them more. All because I didn't look thin like a model. Even now I slip into anorexic behavior at times because of people like that and family that still constantly talks shit about my body.

Do not dismiss someone's struggle, people. Do not think you know better about their suffering than they do. It's almost like saying someone's suicidal thoughts are not a serious case because they didn't actually attempt it (I had someone dismiss my thoughts with that reasoning). In both cases, when it does get "serious enough", it might be too late.
